Hello everyone, I’m a PhD student (hopefully not a student for much longer) in cryptography. I’ve recently become interested in formal verification/type theory etc which brought me here.

I’m generally interested in using Lean to build dependent-typed DSLs for cryptographic applications (such as SNARKs for example). I’m interested in lean both as a theorem prover but also potentially as a somewhat more general purpose programming language for cryptographic implementations. As such, I’m very interested in learning more about writing performant code in Lean. Glad to meet you all!
Hey! Great to see more cryptographers interested in Lean.
Are you aware of https://www.hacs-workshop.org?
if you haven’t seen it, there’s ArkLib, clean, zkLean
@Wrenna Robson I am, thank you! I will be at RWC this year, so I did apply to attend this workshop
I'll see you there

Tanner Duve said:

if you haven’t seen it, there’s ArkLib, clean, zkLean

I was aware of Galois' zk dsl, but I was not aware of 'clean', that looks really interesting, thank you!

I've been contributing to the clean project for a while. There's also cryptography involving reduction proofs. I formalized a recent FRI round-by-round soundness proof (by a colleague and his coauthors) with the help of Harmonic's Aristotle: https://blog.zksecurity.xyz/posts/simple-rbr-fri/

Wrenna Robson said:

I'll see you there

Alas, they did not accept my self nomination, but perhaps I'll see you at RWC itself!

Hi, I’m learning Lean and I was wondering what the state of cryptography in Lean is. How can one contribute? Would it be possible or make sense to eventually create some kind of usable crypto library like OpenSSL?
I think it is possible - but I think it's a little way away.

There's currently efforts underway to bind OpenSSL to Lean by the FRO if it's just about having a crypto library that you can use for programming purposes.

If you are interested in writing a crypto library in Lean while that is possible and I think it can be extremly useful to verify one, using it for execution purposes can be quite dangerous because the Lean compiler certainly does not care about things like constant time execution etc. so you can easily write timing side channels. An approach that would be secure here is to either verify a crypto library written in another language like e.g. Rust with Aneas, or alternatively define a DSL that emits to another language and work with the semantics of that DSL.
Yes - I think a functionally correct one would be great but I do not thing it can be secure per se.

Thank you for your answers @Wrenna Robson @Henrik Böving ! So does Lean not support constant time execution or just not check for it? I did not know about Aeneas but it seems interesting, as I’d like to look into formal verification of cryptography (and how Lean can help)

The Lean code generator has no guarantees that the code you put in is going to produce constant time output and will liberally optimize it. But it is very much capable of outputting constant time code of course
There are in theory ways you could do type things to help with constant time code. But they would require some changes to the compiler/code generator I think.
Way beyond my skill.
So one could write constant time code in Lean but it would be out of the scope of compiler verification? Wouldn’t that happen as well when verifying rust code with Lean via Aeneas?

No that's not what I'm saying. Lean's own code generator that compiles Lean code to C code does not undertake efforts to preserve constant timed-ness. But of course if you want to verify a program written in some language where you get certain kinds of guarantees (notably you do not technically get all the guarantees you need in Rust or even C and might have to fall back to raw assembly at certain points but you can of course also verify that with Lean) you can totally do whatever proofs you want.
Oh okay, I understand now. Thank you!

Hey, I am Mukesh Tiwari, a research engineer working on MPC and blockchains. I recently got interested in formal verifications and would love to learn more here.

@cmlsharp @Wrenna Robson Hope to see you guys at RWC.
